methods.notes: Boards advertise the e659f300 service; the device name is typically serial-based. The f3fd characteristic holds a user-set custom name.

device.name: Onewheel (V1 / + / XR / Pint / GT)
device.notes:
The Onewheel self-balancing board (V1, +, XR, Pint, GT) is controlled over BLE with a rich per-attribute GATT (not a UART tunnel). Fully local, no cloud. Future Motion is hostile to third-party clients — firmware >= 4034 will not stream telemetry until the client answers a keyed challenge — so the community pOneWheel app implements the published unlock handshake to keep local control.
GATT: service e659f300-ea98-11e3-ac10-0800200c9a66; every characteristic shares the e659fXXX-ea98-11e3-ac10-0800200c9a66 pattern:
  f301 serial, f302 riding mode, f303 battery %, f30a odometer, f30b speed
  RPM, f30c lighting mode, f30d/f30e front/back lights, f30f status/error,
  f310 controller temp, f311 firmware revision, f312 current (A), f313/f314
  trip total/regen Ah, f315 battery temp, f316 battery voltage, f317 safety
  headroom, f318 hardware revision, f319 lifetime odometer, f31a lifetime Ah,
  f31b battery cells, f31c last error, f3fd custom name.
  f3fe UART read, f3ff UART write — used for the firmware unlock handshake.

UNLOCK HANDSHAKE (firmware revision >= 4034, from pOneWheel): read a challenge from f3fe, take challenge bytes [3..19), append the published static key D9255F0F23354E19BA739CCDC4A91765, MD5-hash it, prepend the magic bytes 43:52:58 ("CRX"), append the digest, compute an XOR checksum over the buffer, and write the response to f3ff. Without this, firmware >= 4034 will not stream telemetry. (The static key is a hardcoded shared secret published in the pOneWheel source — Future Motion's gate is security-through-obscurity.)

openness.notes: Future Motion publishes nothing and actively locks firmware and litigates against clones; the GATT map and the unlock handshake were reverse- engineered by the pOneWheel community. Documented anyway — expect Future Motion to keep changing the gate.

credentials.notes: No pairing secret. Firmware >= 4034 gates telemetry behind the unlock challenge-response (a published static-key handshake), not a per-user credential. No Wi-Fi. SAFETY: this commands a self-balancing board — treat all controls as advanced.

factory_reset.effect: No documented BLE factory reset; the board stores no network/cloud state. Not transcribed here.

methods.description: Connect, enable notifications on the attribute characteristics, and (on firmware >= 4034) run the unlock handshake: read the challenge from f3fe, compute the CRX+MD5(challenge+static key) response, and write it to f3ff.

steps.action: Connect to the e659f300 service and enable notifications on the desired attributes.
On firmware >= 4034, read the f3fe challenge and write the computed unlock response to f3ff.
steps.expect: Telemetry begins streaming on the attribute characteristics.

setup.notes: Connect over BLE and enable notifications on the desired characteristics; for firmware >= 4034 perform the unlock challenge-response before telemetry flows. No pairing PIN. Confidence high on the GATT map (read from source).

rejoin.notes: No network membership; a new BLE client connects independently.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The GATT service and per-attribute characteristic UUIDs and the firmware unlock handshake are from ponewheel/android-ponewheel's source.

characteristics.name: UART write (unlock response)
characteristics.notes: The unlock response is written here: CRX (43 52 58) + MD5(challenge[3..19) + static key) + XOR checksum. Static key D9255F0F23354E19BA739CCDC4A91765 (published in pOneWheel).

services.name: Onewheel service
services.notes: Per-attribute characteristics (e659fXXX-...). Firmware >= 4034 requires the unlock handshake on the UART read/write pair (f3fe/f3ff) before telemetry streams. See device.notes for the full attribute map and the handshake.
